# Burbank (01, engineer) — SPD-054

## Brief
Make the Bash hook in bin/spud_ledger.py read a trap action string as the shell text it is, so a member's VCS write inside it is refused under Law 7 the way the same write inside eval or `sh -c` already is.

The hole (Agria's proposal, SPD-043): `trap` stores shell code the shell runs later (EXIT at the end, DEBUG before every command, ERR, RETURN, and every signal name or number). analyse_words at the end of its prefix loop only sets a.all_doubt for `trap` and then dispatches it as kind other, so `trap 'git push' EXIT` reaches the hook with no finding. Agria probed it in zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual (the Bash tool's zsh on this Mac), bash 3.2 and sh, with a fake git first on PATH: all four ran git push.

Design, settled by Spud:
- The action string is read as shell text with its own quotes, as eval's rejoined words and a shell's -c string are today (analyse_command / analyse_isolated at depth + 1, deglob'd). A finding inside it is the same finding it would be on the line: `trap 'git push' EXIT`, `trap "git commit -m x" ERR`, `trap 'cd /tmp && git add .' DEBUG`, `trap 'eval "git push"' 0`, `trap 'sh -c "git push"' INT` are each refused for a member with Law 7 in the reason. A trap whose action holds a spud write is a spud call and gets the spud rules.
- The string runs later, at a working directory the hook cannot know (an EXIT trap runs after every later cd; DEBUG before each command). Read the action with the analysis's cwds treated as unknown for the duration of that reading (the way `source` sets a.cwds = None, but restore the line's own cwds afterwards: defining a trap changes nothing on the line). Check what the redirection and path rules do with an unknown cwd and a relative target inside the action for a member; fail closed is the rule, silent is acceptable only where the existing code already treats an unknown cwd that way for other constructs. Say which in your result.
- Fail closed on what the hook cannot read: an action word holding an expansion the hook cannot resolve exactly (SPD-043's expansion_word / resolve_expansion machinery: `trap "$X" EXIT` with an unknown X, `trap "$(cat f)" EXIT`, `trap ${X:-'git push'} EXIT`) is refused for a member with the SPD-043 "cannot resolve" reason; a bare `$X` whose value the line assigned for certain resolves as SPD-043 resolves it (`X='git push'; trap "$X" EXIT` is refused under Law 7).
- The forms that run nothing stay silent: `trap` alone and `trap -p` / `trap -l` / `trap -P` (bash 5.2) / zsh's `trap -` list or print; `trap - EXIT`, `trap '' EXIT` and `trap "" INT TERM` reset or ignore; `--` before the action is skipped. Probe the single-argument form (`trap EXIT`, `trap 'git push'`) in bash 3.2, zsh 5.9 -f and sh from a scratch PATH with a fake git before deciding how to read it, and fail closed if a shell runs it as code. Options and `--` are bash's; zsh's trap takes `[ arg ] [ sig ... ]` and `-` only; read both.
- The command word `trap` reached through a wrapper (`builtin trap`, `command trap`, `env trap` is not a builtin and stays other), a glob (`tr?p 'git push' EXIT`, add "trap" to GLOB_COMMAND_SAMPLES so resolve_glob can find it) or a resolved bare variable (`X=trap; $X 'git push' EXIT`) reaches the same branch. Inside eval, a shell -c string, a function body, a subshell or a loop the recursion reaches it once the branch exists; add one test for each of eval and sh -c.
- a.all_doubt after trap stays as SPD-043 left it. Spud (no agent_id) is not refused by any of this. The differential must show no string moving from refused to silent.

Where: bin/spud_ledger.py, analyse_words (line ~8022): the `if cmd in ("source", ".", "trap")` line and the `elif base == "eval"` branch are the neighbours; SHELLS / eval branches show how a nested string is read; GLOB_COMMAND_SAMPLES (~line 5751); ShellAnalysis (~line 6260) for cwds and all_doubt. Tests: tests/test_hooks.py, a new class TrapActionTest(BashHookCase) beside ParameterExpansionCommandWordTest (line ~2829), whose docstring names the ticket, the probe, and the design in the same voice as its neighbours; use the same refused_for_members / findings helpers (copy them into the class or lift them into BashHookCase if both classes then share them). Red first: write the tests, run them and see them fail on the unchanged code, then make them pass.

Verification: the hook's own suite `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest tests.test_hooks -k TrapActionTest`, then the full suite `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (about six minutes, run in the background; 666 tests on main). Re-probe every refused and every silent example of your tests in the real shells from a scratch PATH with a fake git that writes a marker file, so no test asserts a behaviour the shells do not have. Run a differential of the old analysis against the new, as Agria did at SPD-043 and Sieglinde at SPD-046: their scripts lived in their scratchpads and were not committed, so build yours in your scratchpad (the old module from `git show main:bin/spud_ledger.py`, the corpus every string constant in tests/ with .format templates expanded, the two files in tests/probes/, and generated trap templates in every form this brief names, under a member and under Spud), list every string whose verdict changed, and report its counts in your result: strings changed, each intended, and none from refused to silent. The recipe is in ledger/teams/SPUD-043/Agria.md's log.

Done when: TrapActionTest is red first and then green; the full suite passes with no new failure; the differential shows no refused-to-silent change; `member result` names the functions changed, the test count, the suite count, the probe outcomes for the single-argument form, and what an unknown cwd does to a relative path inside the action.

## Ticket proposals
- **Bash hook: an alias defined on the line and run through eval hides a command (Law 7)** — suggested P2; created as [[SPD-059]] at P2 by Spud.
  Evidence: Probed from the SPD-054 scratchpad with a fake git first on a scratch PATH (bash 3.2, zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual, sh): `alias gp='git push'; eval gp` ran git push in zsh, zsh-nbgq and sh; bash 3.2 did not (it expands no alias non-interactively without expand_aliases). `alias g=git; g push` ran in none of the four, because alias expansion happens when the whole line is parsed, before the alias exists. The hook on this branch reads `alias gp='git push'; eval gp` as kinds other,eval,other with no finding, for a member. zsh's TRAP<SIG> function form (`TRAPEXIT() { git push; }`, `function TRAPEXIT { git push; }`, probed: ran in both zsh readings) is NOT a hole: the hook already analyses function bodies and finds the git push.

## Result
SPD-054 in bin/spud_ledger.py and tests/test_hooks.py, worktree spd-054-trap-string, uncommitted. Two rounds; round 2 closed the coproc'd group Spud's review found.

THE FIX. The Bash hook now reads a trap action string as the shell text it is, with its own quotes, as eval's rejoined words and a shell's -c string are: a finding inside the action is the finding it would be on the line, so a member's VCS write inside it is refused under Law 7, a spud write under Law 6 or the actor check, a database call as a database call, and Spud is refused by none of it while keeping his own checks inside the action.

FUNCTIONS CHANGED, all in bin/spud_ledger.py. Round 1: trap_action_indices, trap_read_index and analyse_trap added beside shell_read_index and python_read_index; a branch in analyse_words after the source branch that appends kind other, runs read_points(option_point(trap_read_index)) and then analyse_trap, which reads each action with analyse_isolated at depth + 1, deglob'd; "trap" added to GLOB_COMMAND_SAMPLES so resolve_glob finds tr?p and tr*p. Round 2: EFFECT_ORDER gained "fork" between "either" and "process"; the coproc arm of the prefix loop now sets max(effect, "fork") instead of "process"; two predicates, builtin_runs (shell, either or fork -- a builtin runs somewhere, so what it stores runs) and builtin_runs_here (shell or either -- and in the line's own shell), replace the bare effect != "process" comparisons, the first guarding the trap branch and the second cd and source; settle is unchanged, since "fork" falls to its else and keeps the directories before the command. SPD-043's a.all_doubt line is untouched.

ROUND 2, the hole Spud found. coproc is not an external wrapper: it runs its command in a forked shell where the builtin does run, and that shell's exit fires the action. Probed in zsh 5.9 -f and zsh -f -o nobareglobqual with a fake git on a scratch PATH: coproc { trap 'git push' EXIT; } and coproc ( trap 'git push' EXIT ) ran git push, coproc { trap 'echo x > rel.txt' EXIT; } wrote the file, and cat /dev/null | trap 'git push' EXIT and { trap 'git push' EXIT; } | cat ran it too; bash 3.2 and sh have no coproc (a syntax error there) and ran nothing for any of them. coproc trap 'git push' EXIT, the simple command, ran nothing in any of the four and is read fail closed all the same. The two pipeline forms were already refused. cd and source under coproc read exactly as they did on main.

UNKNOWN CWD. The action runs at a directory the hook cannot know (probed: trap 'echo trapped >> rel.txt' EXIT; cd /tmp wrote /tmp/rel.txt, and an EXIT action's pwd is the line's last directory; a DEBUG action runs before every command), so it is read with a.cwds set to None, as a sourced file already is. A relative redirection or tee target inside the action therefore refuses a member with the existing 'relative to a directory the hook cannot follow ... use an absolute path' reason, and stays unchecked for Spud -- what the code already does for a source'd file's unknown cwd, not a new rule. An absolute target is checked as any other, and an absolute cd inside the action settles the directory again. The line's own cwds and vars are restored afterwards: defining a trap changes nothing on the line, and the action's assignments run later, where a.all_doubt already doubts every variable, so SPD-043's X=ls; trap 'X=git' DEBUG; $X push keeps its 'may not hold' reason and X=git; trap 'X=ls' DEBUG; $X push keeps Law 7.

SINGLE-ARGUMENT FORM, probed in bash 3.2, zsh 5.9 -f, zsh -f -o nobareglobqual and sh from a scratch PATH with a fake git: no shell runs it. trap 'git push' and trap git print bash's and sh's usage and set nothing in zsh; trap EXIT resets in bash and zsh and is a usage error in sh. It is read all the same, fail closed, at no real cost, since the word names code and the line is a usage error where it is not a no-op. The same probes settled the options: zsh has none after trap and takes that word for the action (trap -P EXIT ran -P at exit, trap -p EXIT ran -p), so both positions are read; trap, trap -p, trap -l, trap -lp, trap -, trap - EXIT, trap '' EXIT, trap "" INT TERM and trap -- - EXIT stay silent.

TESTS. TrapActionTest, 11 methods, beside ParameterExpansionCommandWordTest. Red first in both rounds: 8 of the 10 round-1 methods failed on the unchanged code with 155 subtest failures (the two that pin today's silent readings and SPD-043's doubt passed red and green), and the round-2 method failed 8 subtests on the round-1 code. Green now, and no existing test needed changing (ParameterExpansionCommandWordTest still 11 OK). Full suite: Ran 677, OK (666 on main plus 11), run three times, the last on the final code.

PROOF. Every refused and silent example re-probed in the four shells, 107 strings, fake git/spud/sqlite3 on a scratch PATH: 0 holes (no silent example runs a Law 7 verb) and 21 refusals where no shell ran anything, each justified in the log -- 6 option shapes, 2 single-argument forms, 6 unresolvable expansions, coproc trap as a simple command, 1 member path rule, 2 SPD-043 doubt cases; tr?p/tr*p and bash -lc turned out not to be over-refusals (with a file named trap beside them all four ran git push, and bash -lc ran the action with the real git after its login profile reset PATH). Differential of main's module against the branch over 6,334 commands (every string constant in tests/, %s templates filled, tests/probes/, generated trap templates in every form the ticket names, coproc, pipeline and wrapper contexts, and 18 cd and source control lines), for a member and for Spud: 399 verdicts changed, every one silent to deny, zero refused-to-silent, zero errors. 398 are a member's (183 Law 7 git push, 89 a relative redirect inside the action, 37 git commit, 37 Law 6 --as spud, 36 git add, 8 unresolvable expansions, the rest path and actor refusals), 7 of them naming coproc and all trap-under-coproc; no cd or source line moved.
